title: 📐 Area of a Triangle Using Coordinates
hook: You have three corners of a triangle on a map: (2, 1), (6, 1), and (4, 5). Without drawing it, can you find its area? There's a neat formula using just the coordinates!
explanation:
Area of a triangle with vertices (x₁,y₁), (x₂,y₂), (x₃,y₃):

Coordinate Area Formula
Area = ½ |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|
Always take the absolute value (|...|) — area can't be negative!
Collinearity test: If Area = 0, the three points lie on the same line (they're collinear).
💡 Tip: Memory trick: Write coordinates as columns, multiply diagonally right−left, take half the absolute difference.
worked_example:
Example: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (4, 6), (7, 2).

1
Label coordinates
(x₁,y₁)=(1,2), (x₂,y₂)=(4,6), (x₃,y₃)=(7,2)
2
Apply formula
Area = ½|1(6−2) + 4(2−2) + 7(2−6)|
3
Compute
= ½|4 + 0 + (−28)| = ½|−24| = ½ × 24 = 12 sq units

try_this.question: Check if the points (1, 2), (3, 6), and (5, 10) are collinear.
try_this.hint: Find the area. If it's 0, they're collinear.

fun_fact: This formula is actually the 'Shoelace Formula' — named because the cross-multiplication pattern looks like lacing up a shoe!
